input: What changed in the most recent FOMC statement compared with the previous one?

output.answer: In the October 28, 2026 statement, the FOMC held the federal-funds target range at 3¾–4%, whereas in the September 16 statement it had raised the range by 25 basis points to that level. The assessment of economic activity became more upbeat, changing from “solid” to “strong,” and the forward-looking inflation language changed from saying the September action would support a timelier return to 2% to saying the Committee needs more information to determine the appropriate policy stance. The vote also changed from unanimous approval (12–0) to 10–2, with Lisa D. Cook and Beth M. Hammack dissenting in favor of a 25-basis-point increase.
caveats: This compares the statements released on October 28 and September 16, 2026; it does not incorporate the minutes or any subsequent December policy decision. The Federal Reserve calendar listed the next meeting for December 8–9, 2026 as of October 28.

output.question: What changed in the most recent FOMC statement compared with the previous one?

key_facts.fact: The October 28 statement maintained the federal-funds target range at 3-3/4 to 4 percent; the September 16 statement had raised it by 1/4 percentage point to that range.
The economic-activity description changed from “expanding at a solid pace” to “expanding at a strong pace.”

The inflation-policy sentence changed from saying the prior action would support a timelier return to 2 percent to saying that more information would help determine the appropriate policy stance for a timely return to 2 percent.
The approval vote changed from 12–0 in September to 10–2 in October; Cook and Hammack preferred a 1/4-point increase.
